personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: I ship quick wins for customers and I don't master the technical harness, so a wrong stop in a repository I've never opened would leave me stuck.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: One set of laws across all my repositories helps me ship from one idea, though a hard stop could slow me down.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: This keeps the teams cohesive: the same rule reaches every repository, and it actually stops a spec.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: It is plain files in Git rather than more fluff, but a model deciding what stops a PRD still sounds like a gimmick to me.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: Checking the spec before any code exists could catch slop early, as long as it never touches my code.

objection.text: I ship quick wins for customers and I don't master the technical harness. If a model's wrong call stops my PRD and the only way out is a pull request in a plan repository I've never opened, I'm stuck.

rounds.fit: Fits the lead engineer best and the PM who does not master the harness worst, until the amend action was added.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: The red tells me why in plain words and gives me one action, Ask to amend this law, though I still wait on the PM.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: As the PM I own the laws, and the spec tells me which ones it meets before anyone builds.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: The verdict is kept and shows what was judged, so I can read the board and trust it; the unjudged case stays visible.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: A finding needs a word-for-word quote and a cited law, which is less fluff than I feared.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: No check on code, so it cannot put bugs in production through my work.

rounds.fit: Every persona scores 3 or above on the written spec; the wrong-red risk is named in Risks.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: A red names the law, its reason and the words it quarrels with, so I know what to change, though I still depend on someone to amend a law I disagree with.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: The rules now stop a spec on the page before any code is written, and the reason is on screen.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: Only a CODEOWNER can change a law and agents read the same laws, so the rule that stops a spec is the rule the team keeps.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: The laws are plain files in Git and the verdict quotes the spec, which I can check; a model still decides what counts as a break.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: A stop that shows the quote and the law, and goes neutral when the judge fails, is less likely to block me on slop.

rounds.fit: Every persona scores 3 or above on what shipped; the wrong-red risk stays a person-amended law, as the spec says.
